_doc: TRACK A -- THE RESONANT PARK TAP.  Every number MEASURED unless labelled DERIVED or ASSUMED. Decks are TEXT PATCHES of the committed qal/recov/skeptic/sk_best.cir (gen.py prints every removed/added line). Own PYMS_VAE_CACHE .../vae_cache_parkA built from scratch.  Extractor pk.py WRAPS the committed skeptic extractor qal/recov/skeptic/sk.py, so every completeness metric is computed by already-audited code.

fresh_rerun_with_my_own_cache.deck: pa_base.cir, byte-identical to the committed sk_best_long.cir except one added .print column V(mid)
fresh_rerun_with_my_own_cache.verdict: PASS to the digit -- 0.000e+00 on all 22 metrics

a_instrument_check.independent_cross_check: tap energies re-derived by trapezoid integration of I=(V(source)-V(gate))/25 from the printed node voltages, a path that never touches a 1F integrator: agrees with the 1F instrument to 0.19% on E_gt and 0.08% on E_gtp, and the trapezoid ledger E_source - E_Rseries - E_into_gate_node closes to <= 1e-11 % on EVERY row.

MEASURED_from_the_committed_prn.THE_STRUCTURAL_RESULT: the required park window is EXACTLY the complement of the conduction window inside the beat.  A beat-rate park signal therefore has ZERO timing margin BY CONSTRUCTION: it must switch precisely at both boundaries.  Margin can only be bought by shortening the conduction window (slower beat / faster hop) or by halving the park's rate.
MEASURED_from_the_committed_prn.gtp_tap_misses_by: +8.644 ps late at close (harmless, it must be late) and +8.841 ps late at release (FATAL: still conducting 8.84 ps into the next beat's transfer)

b_what_the_waveform_says_BEFORE_any_deck.why_a_fundamental_rate_tap_cannot_be_nar: the flat-top harmonic sum is duty-locked near 50% for any sane threshold; reaching the 27.2% duty the single-hop fixture needs requires a normalised threshold x=0.8129, i.e. a tap amplitude of 2.94-5.61 V and a minimum of -4.88 to -9.73 V on a 1.5 V-rated gate oxide.  DERIVED, absurd.

d_ELIMINATE_no_park_at_all.deck: pa_nopark.cir (the patch is ONE removed line: XPK)
d_ELIMINATE_no_park_at_all.BUT: the un-parked ring NEVER DAMPS and the delivered rail bleeds.  Measured over a 2500 ps run: max|V(sw)| 0.8382 -> 0.8190 (2 ns, essentially undamped), bank A pk-pk 0.535 -> 0.509, and V(bkb) 0.68155 (811 ps) -> 0.67532 (2500 ps) = -3.6 mV/ns = -2.1 mV per 580 ps beat, versus -0.12 mV/ns with the committed park (30x).
d_ELIMINATE_no_park_at_all.H2: FAIL -- droop 2.812 mV worse than the committed baseline against a pre-registered 1.0 mV allowance
d_ELIMINATE_no_park_at_all.VERDICT: the park is STILL REQUIRED under the resonant drive.  The swsweep requirement is NOT relaxed by resonant gate drive.  This answers the brief's cheapest-possible-park question with a measurement: NO.

d_MERGE_park_gate_on_the_existing_gtp_ta.deck: pa_merge.cir (VPK deleted, VPKM gtp pk 0 inserted as a 0 V series meter)
d_MERGE_park_gate_on_the_existing_gtp_ta.all_gates: FAIL (VBEND 0.077141, VA_open 0.38043, cells FAIL, cut order FAIL, IPK 368.6 uA vs 198.0)
d_MERGE_park_gate_on_the_existing_gtp_ta.MEASURED_mechanism: the merged park is ON at t=0 (V(pk)=V(gtp)=1.1014) and does not release until 137.717 ps. It pulls sw to ground through the transfer inductor, so bank A collapses BEFORE the hop: V(bka) 1.0000 (0 ps) -> 0.7965 (20) -> 0.5119 (50) -> 0.2832 (80) -> 0.1712 (100) -> 0.0374 (137.7). 96.3% of bank A is gone by the time the park lets go.
d_MERGE_park_gate_on_the_existing_gtp_ta.SECOND_defect_independent_of_the_fixture: even with a perfect fixture the merge is make-before-break: the transfer nMOS turns on at 128.865 ps, 8.841 ps BEFORE the merged park releases at 137.706 ps.
d_MERGE_park_gate_on_the_existing_gtp_ta.PA_P1_FALSIFIED: my pre-registered break-before-make argument reasoned about the pMOS threshold (gtp < Vbkb-|Vtp| ~ 0.18 V).  That is the wrong device: at the start of a beat bkb is ~0, so the pMOS cannot conduct at all and the transfer is opened by the nMOS (gt), whose threshold sits at the SAME 0.45 V level on a roughly anti-phase tap. Break-before-make is therefore NOT guaranteed by threshold ordering.  Prediction refuted by measurement.
d_MERGE_park_gate_on_the_existing_gtp_ta.VERDICT: MERGE FAILS.  The free park does not exist.

c_SUB_HARMONIC_a_fourth_mode_at_BEAT_ove.why: the fixture needs the park LOW for 422 ps and HIGH for the rest; no beat-periodic signal can do that (see the structural result above), so the park needs a mode the existing 3-mode network does not have.  The cheapest is one sub-harmonic at f/2 (period 1160 ps): L = 4*L1, i.e. 23.6 nH at B=64, still ONE inductor chip-wide, still shared by every bank, still NO switch and NO new gate anywhere.
c_SUB_HARMONIC_a_fourth_mode_at_BEAT_ove.rows: pa_sub (off 0.45, peak 1.5, 50% duty, Vtn crossing 452 ps), pa_sub_e (crossing 430), pa_subn (off 0.30, peak 1.5, 46% duty, crossing 430), pa_sub2 ({f/2,f} two-mode), plus 0.5/1/1.5/2/3 um park sweeps
c_SUB_HARMONIC_a_fourth_mode_at_BEAT_ove.the_narrowed_tap_is_a_net_RECEIVER: E_park = -0.0398 fJ on pa_subn: the park tap, like the gt tap, HARVESTS from the swinging sw node through the park nMOS's own gate-drain overlap.  Trapezoid -0.039758, 1F -0.039290, ledger closes to 1.2e-11 %.
c_SUB_HARMONIC_a_fourth_mode_at_BEAT_ove.but_the_park_tap_also_PERTURBS_the_gt_gt: adding the park device to a resonant tap changes the sw waveform and hence the Miller coupling into gtp.  d(pair) ranges +0.017 fJ (3 um, 50% tap) to +0.577 fJ (1 um, narrowed tap).  The ledger below is ALWAYS pair + park, never the park alone.

d_the_HOLD_test.H1_gate_correction: H1 as pre-registered (V(sw) <= 0.10 V at EVERY sample from park close to tD) is failed by the COMMITTED BASELINE itself (max 0.76501 V), because the window starts before the park's own pull-down transient. That is a defect in MY gate, declared here and restated in two parts, both reported raw for every row: H1a = settling delay (first instant after close from which |V(sw)| stays <= 0.10 V to tD) and H1b = max |V(sw)| after it.  Baseline: 24.0 ps / 0.09859 V.

H3_PERIODIC_two_beat_run_THE_DECISIVE_RE.requirement: the park must RELEASE before the next transfer begins (708.849 ps measured)

committed_ideal_park (pa_base_per).note: NEVER releases -- the committed PWL rises to 1.5 V and holds. When the next beat's nMOS turns on the bank drains straight to ground through the still-closed park: V(bkb) 0.6630 (708.9 ps) -> 0.3457 (750) -> 0.1268 (811.755) -> -0.016 (1000).  FAIL.

H3_PERIODIC_two_beat_run_THE_DECISIVE_RE.FINDING: NO park in this campaign -- the committed one INCLUDED, and in its worst form -- releases in time for the next beat.  The park's RELEASE has never been designed or simulated by anyone here; the committed decks all end the park with a rising edge that never falls.  On a genuine two-beat run that costs the whole bank.

the_TWO_PHASE_reading_DERIVED_not_measur.premise: if alternate pipeline stages hop on alternate beats (cycle 1160 ps per stage, the campaign's own two-phase directive), a stage's bank A is filled by the previous stage one beat earlier, so it holds charge on [-157.85, +128.865] and the stage's park must be ON exactly on [422.150, 1002.150] -- 580 ps, EXACTLY 50% duty at the div-2 rate.  This is an ARCHITECTURAL INFERENCE; this fixture cannot simulate two stages.
the_TWO_PHASE_reading_DERIVED_not_measur.pa_sub_fit: 29.9 ps of overlap with a charged bank A at the tail
the_TWO_PHASE_reading_DERIVED_not_measur.pa_subn_fit: FITS inside [422.150, 1002.150] with 7.88 ps margin at close and 38.40 ps at release
the_TWO_PHASE_reading_DERIVED_not_measur.verdict: the narrowed div-2 sub-harmonic park tap is the correct park FOR A TWO-PHASE PIPELINE, with real margin on both edges.  For a single-phase every-beat pipeline no park of any kind fits (see the structural result).

f_the_complete_ledger.convention: E_total = E_resonant / eta_amp + E_bias, reverse-engineered from the brief's own numbers and VERIFIED: (2.974 + 1.5)/0.351 = 12.747 reproduces the stated 35.1%, and 4.474/x + 2.71 = 12.747 -> x = 44.58% reproduces the stated 44.6%.  E_resonant here is ALWAYS pair + park tap, both trapezoid, integrated over the full 1000 ps deck.

bias_term_IS4_MEASURED.note: gt and gtp reproduce the skeptic's 0.6234 / 1.1837 EXACTLY by an independent trapezoid.  The park figure is integrated over a WHOLE sub-harmonic period; integrating it over one 580 ps beat gives 2.26 fC, which is a half cycle of swing, not a DC component -- a metering trap I hit and corrected.
bias_term_IS4_MEASURED.still_unmeasured: the two non-rail reference LEVELS themselves (0.85 V, 0.41 V, 0.30-0.45 V) cost area and quiescent power that no deck in this campaign has ever metered

g_ideal_source_inventory_AFTER_the_round.IS1_park_driver: CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT.  0.34-1.32 fJ on a resonant tap (and -0.04 fJ, a net receiver, on the narrowed tap) against the 15.0-15.5 fJ real conventional driver and the 9.7727 fJ headroom.  The park term is no longer the binding constraint.
g_ideal_source_inventory_AFTER_the_round.IS2_sustaining_amplifier: STILL ASSUMED (track B).  This round LOWERS what it must achieve: 27.6-37.9% instead of the previously restated 35.1-44.6%.
g_ideal_source_inventory_AFTER_the_round.IS3_the_NETTING_of_the_gt_and_gtp_taps: NEW, and now the LARGEST unexamined term in the headline.  The 2.974 fJ pair is the arithmetic sum of a -2.749 fJ net EXPORTER and a +5.723 fJ net IMPORTER that are two electrically unconnected ideal sources in the deck.  Summing them books a lossless bidirectional common tank that has never been built.  E_pair(eta_net) = 5.723 - 2.749*eta_net: 2.974 at eta_net=1, 4.349 at 0.5, 5.723 at 0.  The 2.749 fJ swing is 28.1% of the entire park headroom and it sits INSIDE the number everyone treats as closed.
g_ideal_source_inventory_AFTER_the_round.IS4_tap_DC_bias: MEASURED this round for the first time as a per-cycle net charge on all three taps (2.3205 fC/hop -> 2.234-3.481 fJ).  The non-rail reference LEVELS remain unpriced.
g_ideal_source_inventory_AFTER_the_round.IS5_harmonic_synthesis_and_phase_network: STILL BOOKED AT ZERO.  Now worse: this round adds a FOURTH mode (f/2) and a third independent tap phase.
g_ideal_source_inventory_AFTER_the_round.IS7_VHI_pMOS_n_well_rail: RE-MEASURED.  4.129 fJ at one beat, 4.494 at 1000 ps, 4.278 at 1160 ps, 4.022 at 2500 ps -- it is a STANDING cost of ~4.0-4.5 fJ/hop, not a transient that returns, and with ad/as/pd/ps dropped by sg13lv_compat.sp it is a LOWER BOUND.  It still has no home in either the hop or the timer ledger.  If it belongs in E it costs ~4 fJ and pushes R-A at eta_amp 0.5 + worst bias from N_min 60.3 to 66.3 (EXCLUDED).
g_ideal_source_inventory_AFTER_the_round.IS8_the_park_RELEASE: NEW.  Not an ideal SOURCE but an unbuilt REQUIREMENT: every park in this campaign ends with a rising edge that never falls.  On a two-beat run that destroys the bank.  See d_the_HOLD_test.

h_verdict.park_term: SOLVED ON ENERGY.  A resonant park tap costs 0.34-1.32 fJ/bank/hop measured (and can be a net receiver), against a 9.7727 fJ headroom and a 15.0-15.5 fJ conventional floor.
h_verdict.best_row_passing_EVERY_pre_registered_ga: pa_sub_w2 -- div-2 sub-harmonic tap (off 0.45, peak 1.5 V, Vtn crossing 452.066 ps), 2 um park.  VBEND 0.688560 PASS, E_hop 7.98053 PASS, VA_open 0.10290 PASS, cells PASS, pMOS-nMOS +1.823 ps PASS, H1 settle 70.4 ps then max|V(sw)| 0.09915 PASS, H2 -27.464 mV (1.438 mV BETTER than the committed baseline) PASS.  E_resonant TOTAL 3.9702 fJ.
h_verdict.best_row_that_also_fits_the_derived_two_: pa_subn -- narrowed div-2 tap (off 0.30, peak 1.5 V, 46% duty, crossing 430.025 ps), 1 um park.  All five gates PASS, H2 PASS, E_resonant TOTAL 3.5122 fJ, park tap a net RECEIVER at -0.0398 fJ, ON window [430.03, 963.75] inside the required [422.15, 1002.15] with 7.9 / 38.4 ps margin.  H1 marginal: max|V(sw)| 0.09997 V but the settle takes 356.9 ps.
h_verdict.measured_trade: park conductance buys hold speed and costs VBEND.  Every park >= 1.5 um pushes VBEND above the pre-registered band's upper edge (0.68941): 1.5 um 0.690168, 2 um (narrowed tap) 0.692229, 3 um 0.690833.  The direction is favourable (more charge delivered) but the gate is two-sided and I have not moved it.
h_verdict.ADMISSION: E <= 12.7467 fJ is CLEARED with large margin on the measured terms: 3.51-3.97 fJ of resonant drive, N_min 51.9-52.4, fpu min-bank-63 PASS, alu_top bush 29/37 = 99.6% of gates, sha_slice bush 4/10 = 87.6%.  It SURVIVES a 50%-efficient sustaining amplifier plus the worst-case DC bias (10.505 fJ, N_min 60.30, PASS).  It FAILS at eta_amp 0.35 with the worst-case bias (13.516 fJ, N_min 63.90), and it FAILS if the IS3 netting is worthless AND the amplifier is only 50% (15.947 fJ, N_min 66.90).
h_verdict.STATUS: CONDITIONAL.  The park door is OPEN and the standing 17.911 fJ EXCLUSION does not survive it.  What now blocks an unconditional ADMITTED is not energy: it is (i) IS2 the sustaining amplifier, still never simulated; (ii) IS3 the tank that nets the gt tap's harvest into the gtp tap, never built; (iii) IS7 the 4.0-4.5 fJ VHI rail with no home; and (iv) IS8 the park RELEASE, which no design in this campaign has ever met on a two-beat run -- including the committed one.
h_verdict.NOT_an_admission_claim: eta is never quoted here.  All figures are fJ/bank/hop.
